topic: impact list for keeping the wide residual through the digital gain (25-bit subtract -> clamp -> gain today)
status: PROPOSAL ONLY. No RTL change made. Protection semantics are the captain's call.

deployed_path_today.feedback_fir.v:99: residual_pcm <= bypass ? microphone : difference_limited   // CLAMP HERE

proposed_change: carry the 25-bit difference unclamped out of feedback_fir and apply the digital gain to it; clamp only after the gain, where the existing gain_clip path already sits. Because the digital gain is <= 1.0 in every allowed setting, a residual that exceeds 24-bit by a few percent lands back inside 24-bit after scaling, so the information is not lost.

modules: src/rtl/feedback_fir.v (widen residual_pcm, move difference_clip out of the residual path)
src/rtl/audio_pl_replay.v (multiply the wide residual; derive the overflow counter after the gain)
interfaces: feedback_fir.residual_saturated: semantics change from 'pre-gain overflow' to 'pre-gain overflow observed' and must not by itself trip the guard
audio_pl_replay.saturation_counts: the upper 16 bits currently carry residual_clips; their meaning changes
counters: gain_clip_count stays and becomes the authoritative post-gain overflow count
capture: memory packing is {reference, microphone, prediction, residual} = 4 x 24 bit (audio_pl_replay.v:170); a 25-bit residual breaks the 4 x 24 layout, so either the word widens or the capture stores the clamped value plus a separate wide flag
any change breaks existing npz readers, so the driver must be versioned together
driver: the guard must be re-specified: today it stops on residual_clips, which under the new path can fire while the signal is still recoverable
timing: the multiply is currently signed 24 x 16 -> 41 bits; a 25-bit operand makes it 42 bits, one extra bit into the DSP48 cascade
must be re-verified by synthesis and by the existing feedback_fir testbench before any board run
rollback: keep v2 bitstream audio_replay.bit 61bb71aa in place until the new bitstream passes the same tests
board/audio_replay/rollback-v1 already holds the v1 driver; add the v2 driver as the second rollback point
the successful zero-coefficient configuration today used v2 and must remain runnable unmodified (captain's instruction)

what_this_does_not_do: does not change any protection threshold by itself
does not alter the model or the coefficients
does not claim the change fixes the regeneration seen today
open_question_for_the_captain: under the new path, should the guard still stop on pre-gain overflow (safer, but fires during loud speech) or only on post-gain clamp (lets the gain absorb it, but the guard then no longer catches a genuinely large residual early)?
